title: -Ycheck:typer does not terminate on if (b) LazyList.empty else Nil, the lub of LazyList and List
oracle: the program compiles in 3 s without -Ycheck; the existing test run/t498 compiles with -Ycheck:all in 2 s on the base and takes more than 100 s (killed) on the integration build
generator: wave4/harness/seeds (Driver.scala, configuration ycheck): run/t498 with -Ycheck:all timed out at 60 s
detail: def f(b: Boolean) = if (b) LazyList.empty else Nil has the inferred result type of the lub of LazyList[Nothing] and Nil.type, a refinement over the common parents with all their members. With -Ycheck:typer (and later phases) scalac stays in a loop that a thread dump shows in Scope.addString calling Symbol.defString for each member of that refined type, with isStructuralRefinement and allOverriddenSymbols repeating for each member; the run was killed after 30 s and 100 s with no output. Vector(1) in place of LazyList.empty finishes in 3 s. No error is printed, so the cost is in rendering or checking the type, not in a reported mismatch. The same happens on the unfixed base and on 2.13.18 for this program, so it is not a regression from the draft fixes; run/t498 only finishes on the base because its lub is computed with an expected type. Only -Ycheck, a debug option, is affected.
fix_sketch: Find the quadratic or exponential step in the check (likely a type or scope that is printed or compared once per member of a lub refinement) and cache it; not diagnosed past the thread dump.
on_base: same for the program in repro; run/t498 itself passes on the base
confidence: needs a second look: the loop is not shown to be infinite (killed at 100 s), and the cause is read from one thread dump
